notes.title: New Tornadoes and Open Source | Beta 1.0.0
notes.content:
[h1]Open Source[/h1]
I wanted to get this out of the way first and foremost. I alone cannot sustain the development of Wild Omission. It's a huge project, and from modeling, to animating, to programming, it's unfortiounatly too much for to do completely by myself at this time. I've actually thought about making Wild Omission Open Source for years, but I think it's finally time to allow the community make contributions and changes. I believe this will be a good thing for the future of Wild Omission, as it opens the doors for modding, community content, and other possibilities that haven't even been considered yet. For information on how to contribute to the development, please see [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3443651186]this article.[/url]

[h1]New Tornado Types[/h1]
Tornadoes now range from F1 to F5 and change in size and damage output accordingly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/44ce80c2a4ce9ce22508a3b5a91460206db0e53c.png[/img]

Changed Toolbar Scroll Behavior
The toolbar scroll direction has been reversed to be more consistent with other games of the same genre. However, you can switch back to the old scroll direction in the options menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/66f2b23c5f1f6b99da0187e50959a0608a83f2df.jpg[/img]

[h1]Small Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Implemented basic backend for clothing.
[*] Added new main menu splashes.
[*] Fixed Monsters.
[*] Opening the Map snaps the cursor to center
[/list]

notes.title: What's Next?
notes.content:
As many of you are aware. It has been a while since I last updated Wild Omission. There are many reasons for this, but I want to assure you that the game is not canceled, nor do I have any plans to abandon it. I have been taking a temporary step back from active development on the game itself, instead putting most of my energy on the planning and design. I've also been going through a lot in my personal life, and needed some time to process things. 

[h1]Plans[/h1]
With all that out of the way I've got some pretty exciting stuff planned for the future. I've had a lot of time to think about the state of the game, and what it needs in order to improve. I think most players would agree that the game is not in a state that could be considered "final". So I've created several lists of features ordered by importance. Do note that all of this is subject to change, and not a comprehensive list.

[h2]Must Have[/h2]
These are features that I simply cannot allow Wild Omission to transition out of early access without.
[list]
[*] Clothing.
[*] Better Weather.
[*] Item Skins.
[*] Better Enemy AI.
[*] Foundation Steps.
[*] Weather Related Items (Rain Collector, Weather Radar, etc).
[/list]

[h2]Nice To Have[/h2]
These are features that would be cool if they were added before leaving early access, but are not necessary.
[list]
[*] Steam Workshop Integration.
[*] Native Controller Support.
[*] Linux Version.
[*] Character Customization.
[*] Voice Chat.
[/list]

[h1]Beta[/h1]
Along with all these cool plans, the next version of Wild Omission will leave the Alpha phase of development, and enter Beta.

[h1]Creative Mode[/h1]
You can set your world to be creative mode from the world menu. Ever since the early days of development, I have been building up an arsenal of cheats to aid with testing. So most of these can be transferred over. This is the most requested feature I have added in recent memory. The Map is a default item given on spawn, just like the Rock and Torch. You can open the Map by clicking while equipped. notes.title: Clearing Up Rumors and Misunderstandings
notes.content:
It seems the last time I addressed this in a blog post I must not have worded it properly. There is now a rumor that I'm abandoning the game. Let me start of by saying this is not true. So here it is in bold [b]NO, I AM NOT ABANDONING THIS GAME.[/b] Now I will explain what's going on for anyone out of the loop. I started working on Wild Omission when I was 16 years old. I worked on it here and there, until it became an obsession. I would go to sleep at night and wake up early just to get back to development. I never thought about anything else. My whole world essentially revolved around this game. I was working 10+ hours a day at age 17, constantly thinking of new ideas, and better ways to implement existing ones. My life was like this for over a year. Until it starting taking it's toll on me socially, mentally, and physically. I had just been working too hard at it for too long. I hadn't been spending as much time with friends as I would like to, I started picking up bad habits to cope with stress, I constantly felt in a rush, and became increasingly out of shape. Not only this, but I realized I had completely stopped doing things I previously loved, such as my music. With all this in mind I decided the best thing for me right now is to take a break to recover, and work smarter, not harder on Wild Omission. And to start making music again. Music provides a release for me because I can channel my emotions into writing a song and it no longer bothers me. It also allows me to be more active.

[h1]Q&A[/h1]
Q: What makes you say not abandoned?
A: Short of me dying, I would personally like to continue working on it.

Q: So ultimately what does all this mean?
A: It means, I'm taking a break, and then I'm going to be working part time on the game.

Q: So how does part time affect updates? 
A: It shouldn't in anyway meaningful, I tend to be more productive in short bursts.

I would like to mention for historical purposes that this update has been rolled back and effectively canceled due to technical difficulties. But will likely be recreated in the future.

[h1]Taking A Break From Full Time Development[/h1]
Edit: It seems this section caused a lot of misplaced concern for the future of the game, please [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2348700/view/4105666832527488721?l=english]read my updated explanation.[/url]

I have put my music career on hold throughout the time I have spent developing Wild Omission. And I feel it's about time I brought it back. So I'm going to be focusing more on music than working on Wild Omission for the foreseeable future. However, this does not mean that Wild Omission is canceled or no longer going to receive updates. You'll notice I didn't say I'm quitting (I don't quit things). Instead I'm shifting my primary focus and attention to my music. notes.title: A Coat Of Wax | Alpha 1.1.2
notes.content:
[h1]Introduction[/h1]
This update is all about [b]stability improvements, bug fixes, and performance enhancements.[/b] It has been a while since I last did an update like this. There isn't really any exciting new features, it's the same, just faster and more reliable. I have taken bad bits of code, striped them out, and replaced it with better code mostly. That being said there are still [b]some new additions[/b].

[h1]Render Distance Slider[/h1]
The [b]render distance is now customizable.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/361a8b3c3a1c81bb346ae2aa1ca6e0949597eba3.jpg[/img]

[h1]Telephone Studios Splash Screen[/h1]
This isn't something that is really too big of a deal. I do think it makes the game feel a little less amateurish though. I feel like there is an expectation that when you open a game, you are greeted with a [b]splash before the main menu[/b]. Telephone Studios is what I (Larch) release games under, It's not really an actual studio with lots of people, it's just me. Releasing games like this makes it easier if in the future I have employees or collaborators.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/57ece9abae296c85089ac866a8d62ad250e2b803.jpg[/img]

[h1]Improved Node Generation[/h1]
I have [b]increased the node generation[/b] across all biomes. So finding stone, metal, and sulfur should become less of a challenge.

[h1]New World Check[\h1]
When the game reads a world file. it will check if the world is [b]newer than the current registered world format[/b], if it's newer it will [b]prevent you from opening it[/b], and possibly corrupting the file. It uses the same system as the one used to detect pre-infinite update worlds. This was implemented for if people might one day play these "older versions" so they [b]don't destroy newer worlds accidentally.[/b]

[h1]Refactoring[/h1]
Not much to say about this without sounding like a nerd. I take [b]bad code out,[/b] and put [b]less bad code in.[/b] This should have resolved the crash I had been hearing about, but if it still occurs let me know by pinging me on the [url=https://discord.gg/RYz5jYXea5]Wild Omission Discord Server[/url], or making a Post on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2348700/discussions/1/]Wild Omission Steam Community Discussion.[/url]

notes.title: Infinite Update | Alpha 1.1.0
notes.content:
[h1]Introduction[/h1]
This is the biggest update Wild Omission has ever received. It has been the result of over a month of hard work and dedication. It completely revamps the world generation. The worlds are now infinite, have biomes, and are completely different from world to world. This update breaks compatibility with worlds made on the non-infinite versions of Wild Omission. For those who still want to play their old worlds the old version will still be playable via the betas tab in the game properties, but the older versions will no longer be supported.

[h1]Infinite Worlds[/h1]
Wild Omission worlds are now infinite. Meaning that you can keep exploring in any direction for ever and the world will keep going. The worlds are also now completely procedural generated, and the odds of seeing the same thing twice are one in a billion. The pre-infinite versions of Wild Omission featured a basic system that only procedurally generated things like trees and rocks. Now everything from terrain height, to ground color, are completely procedural.

notes.title: Triangles! | Alpha 1.0.2
notes.content:
[h1]Future Plans, and Upcoming Pause on Main[/h1]
I would like to get Wild Omission out of early access by the end of next year! Planned additions needed to make that happen include Full Scale Procedural World Generation With Unique Biomes, Clothing, More Enemies, More Weapons, Dedicated Servers, and more! In the near future I'll share more information about these in detail. I also plan on deactivating the demo before the end of the year. I know that goes against what I had said in the past about keeping the demo, however there have been lots of technical changes behind the scenes and its just a lot harder to update the demo than it used to be. As for now I will begin working on Procedural World Generation shortly after this update goes live. During this time I may not release any content updates on main (only necessary bug fixes) I will however, keep everyone updated regarding the development in these devblogs every Thursday. When the world generation is in a playable state, I will release it on a separate branch so you guys can try it out and give me feedback while I continue to develop it. My reasoning for putting it on a separate branch until it's done is, this is a major change in how the game operates for saving and loading worlds, and it's entirely possible that old worlds won't work initially, but some might want to experiment with it anyways. The plan is to have it so that old worlds will still work once it is released on main, If this is not possible I will let you guys know and provide some kind of alternative. In total I hope to have everything finished by early January, and we can get back to regular once a week content updates on the main branch.

[h1]Triangle Building Blocks[/h1]
Triangle Building Blocks are the latest addition to the building systems in Wild Omission. Very effective at layering and honeycombing, to provide maximum protection from severe weather events. Can't wait to see what you guys do with these!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/b586fb31768f58ffd3bb7aad913dc664391889ba.png[/img]

[h1]Crouching[/h1]
You can now crouch!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/e6ee93ce8017ed285c2a05a5d55f77434512356a.png[/img]

[h1]Splash Text[/h1]
I have always wanted some kind of way to put little messages in the game. Things like trivia, messages, easter eggs, and shoutouts. I wasn't sure how to go about this. Minecraft has a great system, but it's silly to try and copy that when it's something so iconic to that game. Then I got the idea to make something that looks like a little sticker on the main menu, and I'm very happy with how it looks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/e8fec0b52642f476a74bce8835485ca859b0cbd6.png[/img]

[h1]Hammer Improvements[/h1]
The methods used to calculate Upgrade/Repair costs, and Destruction Refunds have been much improved. Everything is now calculated based on a fraction of the crafting recipe for that given deployable. Upgrade Costs used to be calculated by taking a fraction of the upgraded tier's max durability, and using whatever the resource it was made of as the resource. Repair costs were similar in using whatever resource was the "Primary Resource" of the deployable and then charging one of that resource for every one durability healed. Destruction Refunds were similar in using the durability and the same "Primary Resource"

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/1c686f19ecbee9f5b6592a5258baa07aff481591.png[/img]

[h1]Ragdolls Float In Water[/h1]
Gone are the days of losing your things at the bottom of the ocean. Your ragdoll will float!

[h1]Bug Fixes/Small Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Engine stability improvements.
[*] Nodes regeneration has been toned down.
[/list]

notes.title: Alpha 1.0.1
notes.content:
[h1]Community Update[/h1]
It has been awesome seeing all the cool things the community has been doing over the week. The game is finally in early access, and everyone is now able to play. Here are some highlights from the community.

[h3]FloppySword's Gameplay Video[/h3]
[previewyoutube=-YHjMHSwhsU;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Fan Made Unofficial Trailer[/h3]
[previewyoutube=-eqNgeUlzJs;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]rcjoe69 and dmyress's new base[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/a212e7e66dd691545d1b8799a832232b37eb3d55.png[/img]

[h1]Difficulty Settings[/h1]
On the world menu you will now find an option for changing the difficulty of the game. Switching to peaceful will disable all weather, and stop monsters from spawning. You can change the difficulty whenever you load the world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/e9e769a6855a1c6d4ec58a7324466035da4f0e48.jpg[/img]

[h1]Building Privilege Notifications[/h1]
Notifications informing you of your current building privilege status have been added. They will appear when holding a deployable item or hammer. If you aren't in a building restricted zone there will be no notification. if you are, it will either say "Building Blocked" or "Building Privilege" to inform you why you can or cannot place/upgrade/destroy anything.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/1356fc7dfa0f876d4599688cf53e2f45ca357957.jpg[/img]

[h1]Crafting/Inventory Button[/h1]
In the inventory menu you will find a button at the top to take you to the crafting menu. In the crafting menu you will find a button at the top to take you to the inventory menu. This was added to help new players find their way around the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/b3255e216e6fd493374093fd1ffd872164f9d3b4.jpg[/img]

[h1]Thirst/Hunger Changes[/h1]
Dehydration, and starvation kick in a little sooner. They used to kick in at around 5% which basically made them not even an issue worth considering. They will now kick in at around 25%. Further tweaks may be made in the near future.

[h1]Food/Water Changes[/h1]
Various changes have been made to Food and Water items. All meat has been nerfed, bottled water has been buffed, and more have had subtle changes and balancing.

[h1]Improved Node Regeneration[/h1]
The node regeneration has been refined based on player feedback. It now checks if an individual node type(stone, metal, sulfur) is scarce in your area, and regenerates only that specific type. The system used to check the total node count around the player. If there were 0 nodes then it would regenerate in batches or 3-5. This works okay, but if you have harvested all the metal nodes around you, and you are wanting more metal, the only way to get metal was to also destroy the stone and sulfur nodes to get more nodes to spawn. Now if you harvest all the metal nodes, more metal nodes will automatically spawn.

[h1]Demo Changes[/h1]
The demo has been upgraded to same custom version of unreal engine as the full game. A prompt explaining the shortcomings of the demo, and asking the player to buy the full game was also added.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/96386497b0ca48d1d5d6d4f0cceab1b8cee0a07f.png[/img]

[h1]Bug Fixes/Small Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Rename world prompt will now automatically auto fill with the existing world name, this should make it easier to fix typos.
[*] Feedback button now takes you to the Steam discussions.
[*] Fixed Hammer ignoring building privilege.
[*] Fixed low mouse sensitivity braking aim.
[*] Fixed unable to place walls after reloading on demo.
[*] Fixed host parody bug.
[*] World Items shouldn't roll as much as they used to.
[/list]

notes.title: Going Gold | Devblog #29
notes.content:
[h1]Releasing Tomorrow[/h1]
Wild Omission will be releasing into early access tomorrow November 24th 2023! I am genuinely so excited, I cannot wait to see what you all create! When I first started planning out the game in December last year I never in a anticipated the game to do quite as well as it has. It was and still is just my little labor of love game. I make it because it's the kind of game I always wanted to play. It's so neat to see that others are equally fond of it. Thank you all!

This was also a suggestion from the community. It's the perfect addition for your table.

There is now a Large Storage Box. It's like the smaller one, but bigger, with more slots to put things.

Now when falling from a high place, when you hit the ground you will hear a crunch sound.

In the world menu under the multiplayer options, I have added a slider that will let you specify a custom number of maximum players allowed to join your world.

[*] Increased the human ragdoll despawn time from 10 minutes to 20 minutes.
[*] Increased Torch durability.

[*] Changed metal tool node drops to be more useful.
[*] Updated the hammer description to be more accurate.
[*] Updated world items for various items to make them more consistent.
[*] Update item categories of various items to make them more consistent.

notes.title: Authority and Management | Devblog #28
notes.content:
[h1]Tool Cupboard[/h1]
There is a new deployable in Wild Omission. The Tool Cupboard will allow you to control who can build in a certain area. Only players with authorization can build in a radius around a tool cupboard. Tool Cupboards can also be locked, just like Doors and Boxes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/4fb095630f37593f8828149b97a38d62176d9652.jpg[/img]

[h1]World Management[/h1]
I have added options in the world menu that let you rename or delete your world. Along with this most of the UI has received a facelift.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/0a60ca41310d6db83cacc8e6732423adc372bf8b.jpg[/img]

When in Singleplayer, pausing the game, will now pause the game. Previously it would just bring up the pause menu.

[h1]Building Preview Emission[/h1]
The building preview is now emissive. This should make it easier to build in low light environments.

[h1]Small Changes/Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Adjusted volume levels of Torch, Campfire, and Furnace.
[*] Lowered damage zombies deal to buildings.
[/list]

notes.title: Keep Out! | Devblog #27
notes.content:
[h1]Connected Players Menu[/h1]
I have created a menu that allows you to view all people connected to the world you are playing on. You can also view their steam profile by clicking on their name. If you are the host you will have the ability to kick a player who is misbehaving.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/91573439cec630902e28570dcf4247010096e86d.png[/img]

[h1]Code Locks[/h1]
You can now place locks on your doors and storage boxes. You can place them on doors and crates, just the same as any other deployable item. You can press E to set a code if there isnt aready one. If you are not yet authorized and there is a code, pressing E will bring up a menu asking you to enter the code. If you press E and there is a code, and you are authorized, pressing E will bring up a menu that lets you change the code. Changing the code removes all people who were previously authorized.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/8492165dcb9589036b4bf441727d4eee2645b5a0.png[/img]

[h1]Small Changes/Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Zombies now drop leather.
[*] Fixed building anchors becoming occupied after reloading the game (thanks Molly for pointing this out).
[*] Wooden Foundation and Wooden Floor rotation is now determined by player orientation.
[/list]

notes.title: Take Shelter | Devblog #26
notes.content:
[h1]Air Raid Siren[/h1]
I have added an Air Raid Siren, that will warn you of incoming danger.

[previewyoutube=BqO0l8tN_lY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Release Date[/h1]
Wild Omission will launch into early access on the 24th of November 2023!

[h1]Error Messages[/h1]
Previously if there was a connection error, the game would just boot you back to the main menu, with no warning or prompt explaining what happened. I have now added a system for displaying messages if there was an error that required the game sending you back to the main menu. I have waited until now to add this because this should only happen in multiplayer, and shouldn't happen in the demo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/41f3798e6e8094289351baa3d947a778174af119.png[/img]

[h1]Invalid Name Warnings[/h1]
Another quality of life addition is some world creation protection. Previously if you had a world called "My Cool World" and you went to create a new world also called "My Cool World" the game world happily just go right ahead and erase all your progress without warning. Now if you try to name a world the same as an existing world, you won't be able to, and the game will explain that the world already exists. Same thing goes for invalid characters and file names.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/3aeff9e8ab149c922d7f181ef2b1b2a8ee1d3072.jpg[/img]

[h1]Server Version Check[/h1]
The server browser will now only show servers running on the exact same version as you. This is to prevent potential crashes stemming from incompatible versions in multiplayer.

[h1]Bug Fixes/Small Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed Session Host/Join/Leave bugs.
[*] Fixed Spawning in dead and not being able to respawn.
[*] Fixed Master volume option not working.
[*] Fixed rounding error in stair rotation.
[*] Fixed torch effects getting stuck to hands on laggy servers.
[*] Fixed a bug that caused rain sounds to play more than once and get stuck playing.
[*] Fixed crash during world generation breaking save file.
[/list]

notes.title: What happens if strong winds hit your base? | Devblog #22
notes.content:
[h1]New Resources[/h1]
There are several new resources in Wild Omission. The list of new items is [b]Leather, Sulfur Ore, Sulfur, Reinforced Metal, Gold, Charcoal, and Gunpowder[/b]. They are each unique in their methods of obtainment and uses so I'll give them each their own section

[h2]Leather[/h2]
[h3]How to obtain it?[/h3]
Leather is obtained by harvesting animals, it drops with a 50/50 chance of meat or leather.
[h3]What is it used for?[/h3]
None at the moment, but I have future plans for it.

[h2]Sulfur[/h2]
[h3]How to obtain it?[/h3]
Sulfur nodes can be found spawning throughout the world, you can harvest them, or find a collectable sulfur patch, both will yield the ore. Sulfur is also a rare drop when harvesting zombies. You can smelt Sulfur Ore into Sulfur in the furnace.
[h3]What is it used for?[/h3]
Sulfur is a key ingredient in gunpowder.

[h2]Reinforced Metal[/h2]
[h3]How to obtain it?[/h3]
Reinforced Metal is most easily obtained by harvesting metal nodes with metal tools, [b]stone tools cannot gather it[/b]. It is also a rare drop when harvesting zombies. It can be crafted, 15 metal turns into 4 reinforced metal.
[h3]What is it used for?[/h3]
Anything that needs a stronger metal, right now only guns, but more is planned.

[h2]Gold[/h2]
[h3]How to obtain it?[/h3]
Rare drop when harvesting zombies.
[h3]What is it used for?[/h3]
Nothing at the moment, but like leather, I have future plans for it.

[h2]Charcoal[/h2]
[h3]How to obtain it?[/h3]
Burn wood in a furnace or campfire and it will be produced as a byproduct.
[h3]What is it used for?[/h3]
Gunpowder.

[h2]Gunpowder[/h2]
[h3]How to obtain it?[/h3]
Crafted with 20 Sulfur and 25 Charcoal.
[h3]What is it used for?[/h3]
Ammunition, or anything that needs to go [b]boom[/b].

[h1]Item Information Panel[/h1]
If you press the middle mouse button on any item, it will now open a menu that shows you more information about said item. The information includes things like the description, and various stats relating to the item.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/9656975085e7cd8053fef2aa18bc037514953a77.jpg[/img]

[h1]Graphics Options[/h1]
The graphics options menu has been given a slight facelift, to make it match the other menus better. A button has also been added to auto detect the optimal graphics settings for your hardware configuration. The game has always tried to auto detect the optimal graphics settings on first launch; However, it was never calibrated. Now it is, so if you felt the game gave you unreasonable settings, you might want to try clicking the button, assuming you aren't happy with your current framerate and graphics settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/e7f2a81367b83817745520e15ad08e8f325b1194.jpg[/img]

[h1]Improved Wind Damage System[/h1]
I have made improvements to the wind damage system. Previously wind damage from tornadoes was applied to every deployable regardless of there being a wall in between the deployable and the tornado. Now damage is calculated based on a line of sight check. So the more layers of walls and floors you have in your base, the more resistant your house will be to wind damage

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/67235f69402783da614aacc7761f70d22305e54f.png[/img]

[h1]Feedback Button[/h1]
There have been many instances in the past, where a very noticeable bug has plagued the game, and no one has said anything to me. My theory for why this is the case is that, I havent made it clear where to report an issue. All of that changes today, there is no longer a reason not to report an issue. Now on the main menu and the pause menu you will find a feedback button, clicking it will take you to a google form where you can write about the issue and report it directly to me.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/7a907c68e65ae09b4f9cb0eda6a711745aae9ea0.jpg[/img]

[h1]New Artwork[/h1]
I have once again changed the capsule images for Wild Omission. I felt the last one didn't stand out enough against the background of steam so I have created a new one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/e888433848dac8bd76fa71dca1b40d8efb11b870.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/932a4fdb1eb91c25a69115ce4384fcb53c46988f.png[/img]

Fixed chat messages getting stuck on screen(this required completely changing how chat messages work.)

Wild Omission will be taking part in Steam's October Next Fest, this will run from October 9th - October 16th 10AM Pacific. During this even I will be doing live streams, so stay tuned for the dates and times. I will also be chatting with the community regarding the game, and collecting feedback and opinions. There where two patches released earlier in the week, you can read about [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2348700/view/3730725675810838784?l=english]Pre Alpha 0.9.7_03 (Demo Preview 1.3.3)[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2348700/view/3730725675817332015?l=english]Pre Alpha 0.9.7_04 (Demo Preview 1.3.4)[/url] on their respective pages. I have been working in a state of "Full Steam Ahead," and haven't included all changes in this devblog, so instead if you really must know everything that has happened regarding new features and bug fixed please also read the patch notes mentioned above. With that out of the way here are the highlights of the past week of development.

[h1]New Store Branding Images[/h1]
I have changed the branding images on Wild Omission store page. My reasoning for changing them is that, I kept getting the impression that people were under the impression that Wild Omission is just another generic survival game. Wild Omission's primary differentiating feature is its weather system, so I figured I would show it off in the header pictures for the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/fd53b7158e9f12b5badf2cf07dae30d5dfadc5da.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/263d9560f71a59092fc92de75028cfb918a74a0c.png[/img]

[h1]Animal AI Improvements[/h1]
Animals Used to act like they didn't care that you were dealing damage to them. Now they certainly do care very much thank you. They will enter a state of panic after being hurt, they will run around for a few seconds. Along with this all AI creatures (including zombies) should now rotate smoothly, rather than snapping into new rotations.

[previewyoutube=JogzKjRc_r8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Hit Marker Sounds[/h1]
Hit marker sounds have been added. They are triggered when you hit a living creature with a projectile (Player, Zombie, or Animal.) If you land a head shot a different hit marker sound will play. Speaking of headshots, landing head shots now deals more damage than body shots.

[previewyoutube=L7JkKexo2BM;full][/previewyoutube]
[previewyoutube=FDlVnUlHAN0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]New Growable Plants[/h1]
For a while there have been tree saplings. These are a great way to farm trees. However, both cotton and berries have always regenerated on their own. But that changes, now when collecting cotton or berry plants, they will give you two seeds in addition to cloth or berries. These seeds can be planted, and just like saplings, they will grow into mature plants that can be harvested and replanted.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/41b6e59b4d6482e6d4d6d525596d54fb1cb5d3b5.jpg[/img]

[h1]Quick Move Improvements[/h1]
Made it possible to quick move from inventory and toolbar slots.

[h1]Improved Music Playing[/h1]
Music is now tied to time of day.

[h1]Zombie Improvements[/h1]
Zombies will now stop burning if they find shade, or it is raining. There was also a bug with the zombies that allowed them to not burning if you reloaded your save, this has been fixed. There was also a bug that caused zombies to become harmless, this was also fixed.

notes.content:
[h1]Recurve Bow[/h1]
Say hello to the [b]new ranged weapon[/b]. The Recurve Bow is a primitive ranged weapon that deals light damage, and is [b]most effective at short to medium range[/b]. Perhaps the part I found most fun about creating it is the arrow visibility changing based on ammo count. If you equip a bow with no ammo, its arrow will be missing until more ammo is crafting and the bow is drawn. If the bow has an arrow loaded, then it will appear in the view model.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/0cb9d9bd77e2c522ab7a9515eb56e931a60042d9.jpg[/img]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HB2GHA-b0Ek

[h1]Building Hammer Overhaul[/h1]
The Building Hammer has received a complete overhaul. It now has the ability to Repair, Upgrade, and Destroy deployables. You can use the [b]Primary Button[/b] to hit the deployable, if you have the required resource (either Wood, Stone, or Metal) it will [b]repair[/b] the deployable. If you hold the [b]Secondary Button[/b] it will bring up the [b]menu for Upgrading or Destroying[/b] the deployable, simply drag the mouse over the option you want and release and it will preform that action given that the conditions are right. Upgrading will allow you to upgrade building blocks to a higher for cheaper than it would cost to have crafted it outright. Destroying works for all deployables and will give you a slight refund based on the deployables current durability. Previously it only did one thing, deal insane amounts of damage to deployables. This made it a great tool for breaking things if you made a mistake. However what do you do if you want to repair a damaged building block? What if you have a wooden house that you want to make into a stone house? Previously both of these feats where almost impossible, short of just destroying the old one and putting in a new one.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KcF6Uq0ILTY

[h1]Additional Options[/h1]
Two new options have been added. The first is an option to [b]turn off the branding text[/b] that appears in the top left of the screen. The second is an option to [b]turn off the crosshair[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/2a2c020862c35edb5e3b4b178a0b6fa071129049.png[/img]

[h1]Animation Improvements[/h1]
A number of improvements have been made to the animation back end. These changes have no impact that players will notice, but they make programming items much easier.

[h1]Bug Fixes/Small Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed Bug that caused loot crates to spawn with zero durability.
[*] Lowered Durability on Campfire, Wall Light, and Ceiling Light.
[*] Improved Night Visibility.
[*] Made Zombie sounds quieter and less frequent (thanks stormwolf1O1).
[/list]

notes.title: Changes In Pricing
notes.content:
[h1]Why The Change?[/h1]
I would like to start off by bringing some [b]important news to light[/b]. When I started working on Wild Omission back in December 2022 I never expected to get this far. My plan was to release a small free survival game in June. However as time has gone by I have added much more content than I originally planned would be available at launch. to ship for free. For this reasoning the [b]full version of Wild Omission will now be paid[/b].

[h1]What Can I Do?[/h1]
Fear not though, if you still want to play the game for free, as [b]I will continue to maintain the free demo[/b] for as long as there is still demand for it. The difference between the full game and the demo, is that the demo lacks multiplayer, and you can only have one world, and once the game releases into early access the demo might not get updated as often as the full version. If you should choose to upgrade to the full game later down the line, your [b]demo world will transfer over to the full game[/b].

[h1]How Much Will The Full Game Cost?[/h1]
At this time I [b]cannot give an exact amount[/b], because I do not yet know. However I want it to be [b]affordable[/b] enough that the price is not an obstacle.

[h1]Weather Performance Improvements[/h1]
There were some pretty major performance issues with the weather. The main issue is that when the tornado would contact a tree, it would tell it to change its mesh to a stump. This is normal and supposed to happen, the issue is that it would telling the tree to do this every frame, regardless if the tree was already a stump. This resulted in major CPU overhead trying to change the mesh constantly. This has been fixed and the performance is much better. Improvements to storm cloud rendering have also been made.

[h1]Host Parody[/h1]
I have made a change to how player saves are loaded. The game will now always try to match the host save. What this means is that, if I have a world, and I have lots of items in my inventory that are vital to playing the world, and I give my friend the world file, he will load in with all the same items that I had.

[h1]Save Compatibility System[/h1]
I have made many changes to how actors are saved and loaded. Previously if I were to do so much as move a file around, it would risk breaking save files. Now I have created a system that allows for greater compatibility over the long term. It uses lookup tables with identifiers to find the class it needs, rather than pointers to classes, which could change from build to build. Along with this I have created a versioning system for save files, which is able to detect what version the save was last loaded on, and perform any compatibility updates if needed, preventing the save from becoming corrupt. I have already put it into action by changing the location of the sea level, and landscape height. The system was able to correctly reposition all objects to the new ground location. There has also been simular compatibility code added for things like inventories, to detect if the amount of slots has changed since last load, and properly resize the amount of slots without corrupting items. BLAH BLAH BLAH BORING TECHNICAL SPEAK BLAH BLAH BLAH.

notes.title: Devblog #3

[h1]New Direction[/h1]
Ever since I can remember, I always wanted to make a survival game of some kind. It's a genre I have always found fascinating. It's also an interesting technical challenge. There are lots of elements that make up a survival game, from Inventory Management, to Crafting, to Base Building, each element comes with its own unique set of challenges. One thing I knew going into making Wild Omission, is that I couldn't just make some generic [i]Rust Clone[/i] or something, that would be [b]boring[/b]. I needed to make something that was actually unique and interesting for the genre. For a long time I contemplated what this unique thing would be, but it has finally occurred to me that [b]Severe Weather[/b] is something I have found to be an [b]interesting twist[/b] to the [i]over-saturated survival genre[/i]. So with all that said, [u]I'm going to be focusing on making weather a key element of the Wild Omission experience.[/u]

[h1]In-Game Chat[/h1]
I have added a simple text chat to Wild Omission. It allows players to communicate to one another through the game. It also displays a message when a player joins or leaves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/07bb2d52019a432d7f5adbca9b4d98515f11649b.jpg[/img]

[h1]New Clouds[/h1]
A new cloud system has been implemented. It fits the art style better than the stock unreal engine clouds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/7fbe9f6aa6c5c3072376976e21bce68bb286d819.jpg[/img]

[h1]Severe (and not so severe) Weather[/h1]
I spent the past two weeks putting together a complex weather system. It does a lot of things, but it's pretty easy to understand when you break it down. By default it is sunny, but every five to ten minutes, there is a chance for a Storm Cloud to spawn far in the distance. It will slowly approach the island, while also building in severity. If you are lucky the severity won't be too high, and it will just pass over as a really dark cloud. However, if the severity reaches moderate levels the Storm Cloud will start to produce rain and lightning. If you are unlucky enough to have a fast developing Storm Cloud and its severity reaches a peak it will likely spawn a tornado.

[previewyoutube=hwfSnsy6fFE;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Tornado[/h1]
Part of the weather system that I feel deserves its own section is the tornado. It a giant rotating column of cloud. It will suck things up off the ground, deal damage to buildings and plants, and break trees in half. All while not paying a second thought. Luckily they are pretty rare. But if you are unlucky enough to be caught in one you better be in a strong building.

[previewyoutube=IyPDUHAB8Gg;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Devblog #1
notes.content:
Although the game is not currently released, I would like to post [b]updates[/b] here. Just to talk about the things I have been working on [b]behind the scenes[/b], and give you [b]sneak preview[/b] of some of the [b]latest features[/b] I have been working on, however buggy or unfinished they may be.

[h1]Resource Regeneration[/h1]
I have long since had on my TODO list to make [b]resources regenerate over time[/b]. Many playtest we have [i]ran out[/i] of all resources on the island and were forced to twiddle our thumbs. So I have finally gone to work implementing this. Here is a video of the system in action.
[previewyoutube=UsWF95k2Mh8;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]


[h1]UI Enhancements[/h1]
I have spent quite a bit of time going over and polishing the [b]UI code[/b]. It wasn't really all that bad, just kinda all shoved into one class that does [b]way too much[/b]. So I moved lots of things to their own classes and tied up lots of loose ends. I made the [b]server name auto populate[/b] with [b][steamusername]'s Server[/b]. While at it, I also extended the character limit for world and server names. Sixteen characters often just wasn't enough, thirty two should be enough. An option for servers to be [b]friends only[/b] was also added. Not really anything else to say really, just something that needed to be done.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/f04794339d4d4c3ebc3d8f2e71424d038d290de0.jpg[/img]

[h1]Saplings[/h1]
When it comes to [b]trees[/b], rather than make them naturally regenerate, I thought it would be a good idea to add [b]plantable saplings[/b] instead. When chopping a tree, there is a [i]15% chance[/i] of a sapling being given. Once you have one, you can plant them and after some time they turn into a new tree. The system used to give saplings from trees can also be used for other things like giving rare metals when harvesting metal ore, so its pretty flexible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/26c9ce108280ee5d8eb5b1972670c1c07676223b.png[/img]

[h1]Building Improvements[/h1]
I made some [b]improvements[/b] to the building mechanics. During playtests I heard complaints about the [b]wall placement[/b]. Mainly that it was always trying to place at the wall socket closest to you. So I made some tweaks to how the wall sockets behave, it should feel more predictable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081528/aa6becc251a54930f9a45faab6622cabb2f07fde.png[/img]
